dialogue.content: （こんばんは。本日は宜しくお願いいたします。お時間になりましたら始めさせていただきます。）
dialogue.English: (Good evening. Thank you for being here today. We will begin at the scheduled time.)

dialogue.content: よろしくお願い致します。
dialogue.English: Okay, thank you.

dialogue.content: こんばんは、相談員です。はじめに、年齢、性別、今日ご相談したいことをお聞かせいただけますか？
dialogue.English: Good evening, I'm the counselor. To begin, could you please tell me your age, gender, and what you would like to discuss today?

dialogue.content: こんばんは。16歳女子。学校に行きたくありません。
dialogue.English: Good evening. I'm a 16-year-old girl. I don't want to go to school.

dialogue.content: それはとても悩んでしまいますよね…
dialogue.English: That must be very distressing for you...

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: もう少し詳しくお聞かせいただけますか？
dialogue.English: Could you tell me a little more about it?

dialogue.content: はい。高校入学と同時に関西に引っ越してきたんですけど、友達がいなくて辛いです。
dialogue.English: Yes. I moved to the Kansai region right when I started high school, and it's hard because I don't have any friends.

dialogue.content: そうだったのですね。お一人はつらいですよね・・・
dialogue.English: I see. Being on your own must be very tough...

dialogue.content: はい。関西のひと怖いです。
dialogue.English: Yes. People in Kansai are scary.

dialogue.content: うんうん、これまでとは違う環境でとても不安に感じてしまいますよね。
dialogue.English: Mmm-hmm, it's understandable to feel very anxious in an environment that's so different from what you're used to.

dialogue.content: そうなんです。中学はたくさん友達がいたのに。。
dialogue.English: Exactly. I had a lot of friends in junior high...

dialogue.content: 中学の時はお友達と一緒に楽しく過ごされていたのですね。
dialogue.English: So you had a lot of fun with your friends back in junior high.

dialogue.content: うん。中学はいっぱい友達がいました。なのにこっちに引っ越してきてから友達がいなくなりました。
dialogue.English: Yeah. I had lots of friends in junior high. But since moving here, I have no friends at all.

dialogue.content: 今まで仲良くしてきた友達もいない中、きっと、さみしい思いをしてきましたよね。。
dialogue.English: Without any of the close friends you used to have, you must have been feeling very lonely.

dialogue.content: とても寂しいし、辛いです
dialogue.English: I'm very lonely, and it's painful.

dialogue.content: うんうん、それで学校にも行きたくないと感じているのですね。。
dialogue.English: Mmm-hmm, and that's why you feel like you don't want to go to school.

dialogue.content: そうです。みんなは中学から一緒だから仲良くしてるけど、私はそうじゃないから、、
dialogue.English: That's right. Everyone else is friends because they went to junior high together, but I'm not part of that...

dialogue.content: なるほど、そのような状況だったんですね。。それは孤独に感じてしまってとてもつらいよね。。
dialogue.English: I see, so that's the situation... It must make you feel very isolated and painful.

dialogue.content: 孤独だし、中学の友達にも言えない
dialogue.English: I feel lonely, and I can’t even tell my junior high friends.

dialogue.content: うん、とても孤独に感じてしまうのも無理のない状況だと思います。中学のお友達に言えないのはどうしてかな？
dialogue.English: Yes, it's completely understandable that you feel so lonely in this situation. Why do you feel you can't tell your friends from junior high?

dialogue.content: きっと中学の友達は私が元気にやってると思ってるだろうし、私が友達がいないこと知られたくないし
dialogue.English: I'm sure my friends from junior high think I'm doing great, and I don't want them to know I don't have any friends here.

dialogue.content: 中学のお友達に知られたくないのはどうしてかな？
dialogue.English: Why is it that you don't want your friends from junior high to know?

dialogue.content: 友達がいっぱいいたのにこっちで友達がいないとなんか恥ずかしいから
dialogue.English: Because I used to have lots of friends, and not having any here feels kind of embarrassing.

dialogue.content: うんうん、中学のお友達にも相談できずに今日まで一人でつらかったよね。。
dialogue.English: Mmm-hmm, it must have been so hard for you all this time, being on your own and not being able to talk to your friends about it.

dialogue.content: うん。誰にも言えないから辛い
dialogue.English: Yeah. It’s hard because I can’t tell anyone.

dialogue.content: ここまでずっとお一人で頑張ってきたんだね。。ここでは、どんなことでも安心してお話ししてくださいね。
dialogue.English: You've been trying so hard to get through this on your own... Please know that this is a safe space where you can talk about anything.

dialogue.content: どうやって友達作ったらいいですか？
dialogue.English: How can I make friends?

dialogue.content: そうですね、高校でもお友達をつくって学校に楽しくいけるようになったらいいですよね。
dialogue.English: Right. It would be great if you could make friends in high school so you can enjoy going to school.

dialogue.content: 友達が出来たら学校行きたくなると思う
dialogue.English: I think I would want to go to school if I had friends.

dialogue.content: そうだね、とても前向きで素晴らしいね！
dialogue.English: I agree, that's a wonderful and positive way of thinking!

dialogue.content: でも関西のひとなんか怖いし
dialogue.English: But people from Kansai are kind of scary...

dialogue.content: 怖いと感じるのはどんなところかな？
dialogue.English: What is it about them that you find scary?

dialogue.content: 関西弁ってなんか怒ってるみたいに聞こえる
dialogue.English: The Kansai dialect sounds kind of like they’re angry.

dialogue.content: うんうん、そう感じているんですね。
dialogue.English: Mmm-hmm, I see that's how it sounds to you.

dialogue.content: だから話しかけ辛い
dialogue.English: That's why it's hard to approach them.

dialogue.content: そうですね、言葉遣いが違うとなんだか戸惑ってしまいますよね。
dialogue.English: I understand. It can be confusing when people speak differently, can't it?

dialogue.content: はい。方言が全然違うし何言ってるかもわからないし
dialogue.English: Yes. The dialect is completely different, and sometimes I don't even understand what they're saying.

dialogue.content: うん、方言もたくさんあって知らないことが多いと話しかけづらくなりますよね。
dialogue.English: Yes, when there are so many unfamiliar dialects and words, it can certainly make it difficult to strike up a conversation.

dialogue.content: 学校で話しかけてきてくれる子はいるのかな？
dialogue.English: Is there anyone at school who approaches you to talk?

dialogue.content: います。後ろの席の子
dialogue.English: Yes. The person who sits behind me.

dialogue.content: 後ろの席の子とはどんなお話をするのかな？
dialogue.English: What kinds of things do you talk about with the person behind you?

dialogue.content: 好きなテレビとか中学のこととか
dialogue.English: Things like favorite TV shows and stuff about junior high.

dialogue.content: うんうん、そのときどんな気持ちになるかな？
dialogue.English: Mmm-hmm, and how do you feel at those times?

dialogue.content: この子と話してると楽しい
dialogue.English: It's fun talking to them.

dialogue.content: お話ししていて、怖いという気持ちはいかがですか？
dialogue.English: When you're talking with them, what happens to that scary feeling?

dialogue.content: この子は怖くないです。優しいです。
dialogue.English: This person isn't scary. They're kind.

dialogue.content: 後ろの席の子なら、関西弁でも怖がらずにお話が出来きるんですね。
dialogue.English: So with the person behind you, you’re able to talk without feeling scared, even if they speak in the Kansai dialect.

dialogue.content: まずはその子とお友達になってみるのはどうかな？
dialogue.English: How about starting by becoming friends with them?

dialogue.content: うん。その子は優しいから。クラスの男子とかリーダー格の女子がこわい
dialogue.English: Yeah. That person is kind. It's the boys in the class and the leader-type girls who are scary.

dialogue.content: クラスで目立っている子が怖いと感じてしまうんですね。どんなところからそう感じるのかな？
dialogue.English: So you feel scared of the students who stand out in class. What is it that makes you feel that way?

dialogue.content: 目をつけられていじめられないかって不安
dialogue.English: I’m worried they’ll single me out and bully me.

dialogue.content: なるほど、、それはとても不安だよね。。
dialogue.English: I see... That must be very worrying.

dialogue.content: 転校生ってだけで目立つし
dialogue.English: Just being a transfer student makes me stand out.

dialogue.content: うんうん、目立つことで目をつけられてしまうのはとても怖いよね。。
dialogue.English: Mm-hm, it’s very scary to think that standing out could make you a target.

dialogue.content: 後ろの席の子には不安に感じていること、お話できそうかな？
dialogue.English: Do you think you could talk to the person behind you about what you're worried about?

dialogue.content: まだそこまで相談できない
dialogue.English: I can't talk to them about something that serious yet.

dialogue.content: お友達だけど深くないし
dialogue.English: We're friendly, but it's not a deep friendship.

dialogue.content: うんうん、やさしいお友達だけど、いきなり深い話はしづらいよね。。
dialogue.English: Mmm-hmm, even with a kind friend, it's hard to suddenly bring up a deep conversation.

dialogue.content: 嫌われたくない
dialogue.English: I don't want to be disliked.

dialogue.content: うん、嫌われるのはとても怖いよね。
dialogue.English: Yes, the idea of being disliked is really scary.

dialogue.content: せっかくお友達になったから
dialogue.English: Since I’ve finally made a friend.

dialogue.content: うん、うん、
dialogue.English: Mm-hm, mm-hm.

dialogue.content: でももっと友達欲しい
dialogue.English: But I want more friends.

dialogue.content: もっとお友達を作っていきたいですよね。中学の頃はお友達とどんなお話をしたりしてきたのかな？
dialogue.English: You want to make more friends. What kind of things did you used to talk about with your friends in junior high?

dialogue.content: 好きなひとの話とかジャニーズの話とかかな
dialogue.English: I guess we talked about people we had crushes on, or about Johnny's idols.

dialogue.content: 自分の好きなことを話しているととても楽しいよね。
dialogue.English: Talking about things you like is really fun, isn't it?

dialogue.content: 本当はもっと楽しい話いっぱいしたい
dialogue.English: I really just want to have more fun conversations.

dialogue.content: うんうん、きっと高校のみんなも、自分の好きなことをたくさんお話ししたいと思っているんじゃないかな？
dialogue.English: Mmm-hmm, I'm sure that everyone else in your high school wants to talk a lot about their favorite things, too.

dialogue.content: 友達になってくれるかなー？
dialogue.English: I wonder if they’ll be willing to be friends with me?

dialogue.content: きっと前向きなあなたなら、きっとたくさんのお友達ができると思いますよ！
dialogue.English: With your positive attitude, I'm sure you'll be able to make lots of friends!

dialogue.content: 友達欲しいです！
dialogue.English: I want friends!

dialogue.content: うん！その調子！あなたがお友達と好きなことを話していると楽しいと感じたように、お友達の話をたくさん聞いてみるのはどうかな？
dialogue.English: Yes! That's the spirit! Just as you enjoy talking about your favorite things with friends, how about trying to listen a lot to what your friends have to say?

dialogue.content: そうか。聞いてあげたらいいんだね
dialogue.English: Oh, I see. So I should listen to them.

dialogue.content: うん、自分のことも伝えて、相手の話もたくさん聞いてあげると、お互いのことをたくさん知れて、もっとお話したくなると感じたけれど、どうかな？
dialogue.English: Yes. I feel that if you share things about yourself and also listen a lot to what the other person has to say, you can learn a lot about each other and will want to talk more. What do you think?

dialogue.content: うん。そうしたら楽しくなると思う！それなら出来そう！
dialogue.English: Yeah. I think that would make it fun! I think I can do that!

dialogue.content: 中学の時お友達と楽しくやってきたあなたなら、きっと高校でもお友達をたくさん作って楽しく学校生活が送れるようになると思います！
dialogue.English: Since you had so much fun with your friends in junior high, I'm sure you can make lots of friends and have an enjoyable school life in high school, too!

dialogue.content: 今日はそろそろ時間となってしまいましたが、お話してみていかがですか？
dialogue.English: We're almost out of time for today, but how do you feel after our conversation?

dialogue.content: 学校行きたくなかったけど、ちょっと頑張ってみる！ありがとう！
dialogue.English: I didn't want to go to school, but I'll try a little! Thank you!

dialogue.content: こちらこそ、大切なお話をここに相談してくれてありがとうございます。また不安に感じたり悩んだ時にはいつでもここにお話に来てくださいね。
dialogue.English: No, thank you for sharing something so important with me today. If you ever feel anxious or troubled again, please feel free to come back and talk anytime.

dialogue.content: はいそうします！
dialogue.English: Yes, I will!

dialogue.content: あなたの学校生活が良い方向に行くように私も応援しています！
dialogue.English: I'll be cheering for your school life to go in a better direction!

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます
dialogue.English: Thank you.

dialogue.content: では本日はご相談ありがとうございました。終了のメッセージをお送りいたしますね。
dialogue.English: Well then, thank you for your consultation today. I will send the closing message now.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございました
dialogue.English: Thank you very much.

dialogue.content: （クライエント役ありがとうございました。厳しめでも構いませんのでFBでコメントいただけますと幸いです。お疲れさまでした。）
dialogue.English: (Thank you for playing the client role. I would appreciate any comments or feedback, even if it’s on the stricter side. Good work.)

dialogue.content: （カウンセラー役お疲れ様でした。ありがとうございました）
dialogue.English: (Good work playing the counselor. Thank you.)
